decisions.reason: ACE3 was publicly launched as the new industry-standard ALCMS control platform at the core of the firm's airfield lighting business, so heavy investment and visible commitment make continuation very likely.

The air situation display supports the firm's tower and surveillance integration strategy, and pandemic-depressed airport procurement offers a temporary explanation for any weak results, so management persists.
Training programs are low-cost, recurring service offerings tied to the firm's installed base and consultative positioning, and pandemic disruption to on-site training is easily seen as temporary.
The airfield ground lighting course directly supports the core lighting business and its service revenues, so there is little reason to abandon it despite the COVID-related slowdown.
The collaboration software embodies the announced move toward collaborative decision-making and real-time information sharing, so its centrality to the strategy argues for persistence.

The MLAT system was publicly announced at inter airport Europe as a flagship of the firm's surveillance direction, so strong public commitment and sunk R&D make the firm keep it and attribute slow uptake to the aviation downturn.
